drivingQuestion: What follows from the mishna ruling that intent to eat half an olive-bulk and burn half does not combine?
outcomeNote: an inference that the next unit sets against the mishna's first clause

segments.he: לֶאֱכוֹל כַּחֲצִי זַיִת וּלְהַקְטִיר כַּחֲצִי זַיִת – כָּשֵׁר. טַעְמָא דְּלֶאֱכוֹל וּלְהַקְטִיר, הָא לֶאֱכוֹל וְלֶאֱכוֹל דָּבָר שֶׁאֵין דַּרְכּוֹ לֶאֱכוֹל – מִצְטָרֵף;
segments.en: § The mishna teaches: If one slaughtered the animal with intent «to eat half an olive-bulk and to burn half an olive-bulk» not at the appropriate time or in the appropriate area, the offering is «fit.» The Gemara infers: The «reason that» the two halves of an olive-bulk do not join together is because his intent was «to eat» half an olive-bulk «and to burn» half an olive-bulk. «But» if his intent was «to eat» half an olive-bulk of the meat «and to eat» half an olive-bulk of «an item whose» typical «manner» is such that one does «not partake» of it, then the halves do «join together» and disqualify the offering, as both intentions concern eating.
